title: Singleton Pattern
overview: Ensure a class has only one instance and provide a global point of access to it.
useCases: When you want to maintain a single instance of a class globally
Useful when a single shared resource (config, logger, connection) must be accessed throughout the application
When you need to coordinate actions across the system from a single point (e.g. a thread pool or cache)
exampleUses: A print spooler that must coordinate all print jobs from a single queue to avoid conflicting output
An application-wide event bus where all components publish and subscribe through one central dispatcher
A device driver for hardware that must not be initialised more than once (e.g. a GPU context or serial port)
